junction.name: 2 Avenue & East 125 Street, New York City

claims.text: 2 Avenue & East 125 Street had 44 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 9 pedestrians injured, 8 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
These counts are 2 Avenue & East 125 Street's own: the city's record places 84 of the 210 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.0 million a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure).
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south in 43% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 17% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $89,000 a year.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $452,000 a year.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for 2 Avenue, East 125 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 8, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 11.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 8, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 11
Subject: Request for safety study at 2 Avenue & East 125 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We ask you to carry out a safety study at 2 Avenue & East 125 Street for the roads you are responsible for, 2 Avenue and East 125 Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 104 crashes, of which 44 were injury crashes. One person was killed. Nine pedestrians and 8 cyclists were injured. This is a city priority location. In the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm is $3.0 million. No safety work is recorded in this period.

We ask you to consider, subject to a site check and design review:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent about 0.3 pedestrian injury crashes per year, with about $89,000 in harm avoided per year, and to pay for itself if installation costs under $0.6 million. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

* reflective backplates on the traffic signals, expected to prevent about 1.3 injury crashes per year, with about $452,000 in harm avoided per year, and to pay for itself if installation costs under $3.2 million.

Please let us know the findings and next steps.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
